notes.meaning: Pilate refused to change the title on the cross despite the Jewish leaders' complaints. In Roman law and Jewish speech, this phrase meant the ruling was final and could not be altered. God overruled Pilate so that the sign remained as a true public statement that Jesus is the King.

The four Roman executioners divided Jesus' outer clothes among themselves as part of their payment. His undergarment was special because it was woven seamlessly from top to bottom in one piece. This detailed memory shows that an eyewitness saw the crucifixion up close.

Rather than ripping the seamless tunic into pieces, the soldiers gambled to see who would keep it whole. Without knowing it, these soldiers fulfilled Psalm 22, which said people would cast lots for His clothing. God directed every detail of what happened, even while sinful men divided the Lord's clothes.

Four faithful women stayed near the cross of Jesus while He was dying. They braved insults and danger so they could support Him with their quiet love. Their courage reminds us that real love stays close to Jesus even in painful times.

Looking down from the cross, Jesus saw His grieving mother and John, the disciple He loved, standing nearby. He gave Mary into John's care and told John to treat her as his own mother. Even while bearing the sins of the world, Jesus faithfully honored His mother and provided for her future.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching holds that Jesus giving Mary to John shows she had no other children, supporting the doctrine of her perpetual virginity. It also teaches that Jesus gave Mary as a spiritual mother to all believers.

notes.meaning: Jesus knew that His work was almost complete and that every prophecy about His suffering was coming true. Crucifixion brought terrible fever and thirst, so He stated plainly that He was thirsty. His cry showed His real human pain while also fulfilling Psalm 69.

A jar of sour wine sat nearby for the soldiers to drink. They soaked a sponge in the wine, placed it on a stalk of hyssop, and held it up to His mouth. This drink moistened His dry mouth so He could speak His final words with strength.

After taking the sour wine, Jesus announced that His work was finished. He then bowed His head and handed over His spirit to God. This was a shout of victory, declaring that the full debt of human sin was paid once and for all.

The religious leaders asked Pilate to break the legs of the crucified men so they would die before the Sabbath began at sunset. Under Jewish law, leaving bodies hanging overnight would make the land unclean, especially on this great feast day. Breaking their legs kept the victims from pushing up to breathe, bringing death quickly.

The soldiers came and broke the legs of the two criminals hanging beside Jesus. When they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His bones. God protected the body of His Son from harm because Jesus had already laid down His life freely.

To be certain Jesus had died, a soldier pierced His side with a spear. Immediately, blood and water flowed out from the wound. This showed clearly that Jesus had truly died, and it symbolized the forgiveness and cleansing He gives to all who believe.

John personally saw the blood and water flow from Jesus' side and wrote down what happened. He gave this truthful testimony so that those who read it would put their faith in Jesus. We can trust that the story of Jesus is built on real historical facts.

These events happened so that ancient Scripture would come true, saying that not one of His bones would be broken. In the Old Testament, the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed without any broken bones. Jesus is the true Passover Lamb whose death rescues us from judgment.

The soldier's spear also fulfilled another prophecy, which promised that people would look on the One they pierced. Those standing near the cross saw His wounded side, and one day the whole world will look upon Him. Sinners who look to the pierced Savior find mercy and forgiveness.

Joseph of Arimathea was a wealthy leader who had followed Jesus secretly because he feared the other rulers. After Jesus died, he found the courage to ask Pilate for the body so he could bury it properly. When others had run away, God gave this quiet follower boldness to honor Christ.

Nicodemus, who had first come to Jesus at night, joined Joseph and brought about seventy-five pounds of sweet-smelling spices. This huge amount of myrrh and aloes was the kind of honor given to a king's burial. These men openly treated Jesus with royal respect in His death.

Joseph and Nicodemus took Jesus' body and wrapped it in strips of linen along with the rich spices. This followed the Jewish burial custom, which treated the body of a loved one with deep honor. They gave the Savior a loving and dignified resting place.

Near the place where Jesus was crucified, there was a garden with a brand-new tomb cut out of the rock. No dead body had ever rested in it before. Because the tomb was untouched, no one could later claim that someone else had risen from that grave.

The Sabbath was about to begin at sunset, so the men had very little time to finish the burial. Because this clean tomb was so close by, they laid Jesus' body there right away. God guided every circumstance so that His Son received an honorable resting place without delay.
